newsitem.title: USA: SmithKline drug promising for lung cancer.
newsitem.headline: SmithKline drug promising for lung cancer.

text.p: SmithKline Beecham Plc and the National Cancer Institute, Genova, Italy, said Wednesday that SmithKline's Hycamtin, or topotecan hydrochloride, may offer a promising new treatment option for patients suffering from small cell lung cancer.

They said that in one of the largest Phase II trials to date conducted with a single agent in the second-line treatment of this disease, patients treated with Hycamtin achieved a 22 percent response rate.
Hycamtin is currently available for use in the treatment of patients with recurrent, metastatic ovarian cancer.

"This is one of the highest response rates ever reported with a single agent in small cell lung cancer patients who had previously undergone and failed combination chemotherapy with traditionally used drugs," the Institute was quoted as saying in a press release.

"Since results of studies with other drugs as second-line treatment have been very disappointing, there is currently no standard treatment for this patient population. Hycamtin is one of the few drugs in the past 10 years to demonstrate significant activity in treating this devastating disease," it said.

According to the two organizations, Hycamtin was generally well-tolerated and as with many chemotherapeutic agents, the main side effect experienced in this study was suppression of white blood cells produced in the bone marrow, which was predictable and manageable.
The most commonly reported non-hematologic side effects were mild fatigue and malaise.
The study was published in the May issue of the Journal of Clinical Oncology.
